recommendation.summary: dsh-tui 0.11.0 is an interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness, mounted as a Cordis bundle patch over dsh-base. Plugin-owned docs describe one user-facing workflow: the interactive TUI, installed as profile `dsh-tui` (`dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`, then `dsh-tui`/`dst` or `dsh --profile dsh-tui`). No headless, SDK or ACP workflow is documented, so executionProfiles is tui only. Node intent: engines.node is `^22.19 || >=24` in both source and published manifests (declared support for 22 and 24), and the README development section states CI uses Node 24 with pnpm 11, making 24 the strongest author signal (ci-tested) and the preferred major; 22 is retained as declared-support. The development packageManager field pins pnpm@11.21.0; consumer profile installs only require pnpm to be present, which is recorded as a gap. Author DSH baseline: README names DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 as the primary compatibility target and pnpm-workspace.yaml calls the 0.1.7-rc.2 line the primary validated line. Development-only workspace overrides were deliberately not transferred to the host profile. No startup disabling/offline flag of the permitted DSH_<PLUGIN>_DISABLED/OFFLINE/NO_NETWORK form is evidenced, so no limited startup comparison is recorded.

conclusion.statement: dsh-tui 0.11.0 could not be installed into its declared `dsh-tui` profile on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 in either tested Node major. The TUI surface case on Node 24 (dsh-tui-node24-tui) is surface-incompatible: `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` exited 1 with `dsh: installation rejected: Plugin @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.11.0 is incompatible with dsh 0.1.7-rc.2: peerDependencies {"@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry":"0.1.7-rc.1","@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node":"0.1.7-rc.1"}` and `Exact-version exemption: not active`. The Node 22 TUI case (dsh-tui-node22-tui) is unknown: its install stage timed out at 180s after pnpm had already resolved and added the plugin tarball, so no bounded result was produced. Both native cases (dsh-tui-node22, dsh-tui-node24) are install-failed with the same reason, `the traced DSH plugin install command failed`, and the same artifact sha256 6cd8736c87228d91ab237955958f7c4064bff0f695be6e171e53a6ee180bf74d. The failure is therefore not Node-major-specific: it is a declared peer-range mismatch between the plugin's published peerDependencies and the DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 runtime. The plugin's published manifest pins `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node` to `0.1.7-rc.1 || 0.1.7-rc.2` in the source manifest, but the installed resolution demanded exactly 0.1.7-rc.1 for both, which the 0.1.7-rc.2 runtime does not satisfy. No plugin code executed: profile, registration, host, surface, interaction and shutdown stages were all skipped, so no TUI rendering, session, or interaction behavior was observed. This is a dependency/peer-range gate failure, not a rendering or runtime defect, and it is not evidence about the plugin's TUI functionality. The author's own README names DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 as the primary compatibility target, so this mismatch is a genuine finding against the author's stated baseline rather than an artifact of testing an unsupported host. No recovery action was taken: the failure is a declared-range rejection that requires either a plugin-side peer-range fix or an explicit exact-version exemption, and granting an exemption is an operator decision that would bypass the very compatibility gate under test, so it was not attempted. No network route change was needed; the batch ran to completion with exitCode 0 and failedTasks 0, meaning all four scheduled cells were executed and reported rather than the batch aborting.

Web/TUI plane: the declared tui profile was exercised on Node 24 and rejected at install with an explicit peer-range incompatibility; the Node 22 tui cell timed out during install and is unknown, so the TUI plane has no passing observation on any Node major.
SDK/ACP plane: not exercised; the plugin documents no SDK or ACP workflow, so no adapter cells were scheduled (adapterCells 0).

No plugin code executed in any cell: profile, registration, host, surface, interaction and shutdown stages were skipped, so TUI rendering, session management, keybindings, image previews and interaction behavior remain entirely unverified.

The Node 22 TUI install timeout is unresolved: pnpm had already added the plugin tarball before the 180s bound, so it is unknown whether that cell would have hit the same peer-range rejection or a different install problem.

Authenticated DeepSeek credential (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY) and subscription OAuth sign-in via the bundled dsh-auth plugin were not exercised; external accounts cannot be completed on the user's behalf and are recorded as coverage gaps, not compatibility failures.

Collection gaps remain: docs/getting-started.md, docs/plugins.md, docs/README.md, docs/configuration.md and docs/getting-started.en.md were omitted by the evidence byte budget, so full install and profile setup steps are unverified.

The consumer profile install requires pnpm but no exact pnpm version is pinned by the plugin; the runner used pinned pnpm 11.7.0 for Node 22+ while the development packageManager field names pnpm@11.21.0.
Windows-specific behavior (danger-full-access default, approval never, Git Bash discovery for liangshen mode) and platform-specific terminal image/clipboard paths were not exercised.
Launcher subcommands (dsh-tui update/doctor/safe), the /update network check, and the VS Code and Herdr integrations were not exercised.
No exact-version exemption was granted and no operator preset route was changed; the peer-range rejection was left as the observed result rather than bypassed.
